documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
47M here for his regular check on BP and cholesterol. Psoriasis is managed by dermatology and quiet on weekend clobetasol.

No complaints. What's on his mind is lung cancer. He read an article online tying cigarettes to lung cancer, and it talked about risk going up with the dose, which got him thinking about his own numbers. His dad got a lung cancer diagnosis at 55 and died of it at 60. He's smoked about a pack a day since he was 15.

Went over it in plain terms: the more cigarettes a day and the more years, the higher the risk, and it isn't a threshold thing - every pack-year adds. The good news side of the same curve is that risk starts coming down after quitting and keeps dropping the longer he stays off. He listened closely. Not ready to pick a date, but said this is the first time he's really thought about it. CT screening for lung cancer starts at 50 for people with his history; we'll set that up when he's eligible.

Meds: lisinopril 10, atorvastatin 20, olanzapine 10 qhs (psych), ibuprofen prn knee, clobetasol oint.
NKDA.

Exam: BP 130/85, HR 78, RR 16. No distress. No cervical or supraclavicular nodes. Lungs clear throughout, good air movement. Heart regular. No clubbing. Knee unchanged.

A/P
- HTN: fine, continue lisinopril.
- Lipids: fasting panel today on atorvastatin 20.
- CBC today.
- Tobacco: as above. Offered help any time - meds, quit line, both.
- COVID vaccine: eligible now, he's booked at the pharmacy next week.
- Colon screening: he'd like to do it after the summer.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood count is normal. Cholesterol: LDL 120, HDL 45, triglycerides 250. The triglycerides jumped since last year - sweets, white bread and beer all push that number. Worth cutting back where you can. We'll recheck at your physical.

documents.title: Smoking Cessation Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seeing him today for my colleague. 47 y/o with HTN, high cholesterol, metabolic syndrome, schizophrenia (stable), here because he wants to quit smoking - follows on from the April conversation about lung cancer.

Still 1 ppd, has been since he was 15. Tried patches and gum more than once; each time the cravings and the irritability got him and he was back within a few weeks. Says this time he means it: he just became a grandfather and wants to be around and healthy. Two things matter to him: he doesn't want to put on weight, and he doesn't want anything that messes with his sleep - a friend told him one of the quit pills gives you awful dreams.

Screening: no depression now, no seizures ever, no eating disorder. Schizophrenia has been stable for years on olanzapine with his psychiatrist. No head injury. BP and cholesterol controlled on his meds. Drinks socially, weekends.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI 28. Alert, engaged, linear. Lungs clear.

A/P
Tobacco dependence, motivated.
- Bupropion XL 150 mg each morning. Talked about how it works on cravings, tends not to add weight, and taking it in the morning keeps it away from bedtime. Quit date in about 10 days once it's on board.
- Pair with the quit line; number given. Plan for triggers (first cigarette with coffee, the drive home).
- Will let his psychiatrist know he's starting it.
- RN call in a month.
- Flu shot today.

BP/lipids: no changes.

documents.title: Message to psychiatry
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Left a voicemail and faxed a note to his psychiatrist: started bupropion XL 150 daily today for smoking cessation, olanzapine unchanged, asked them to call if they have concerns.

documents.title: Cessation follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called as planned. On bupropion XL 150 each morning, no side effects, sleeping fine, mood steady. Didn't make it all the way on his quit date but is down to about 10 cigarettes a day from a pack. Hardest time is after work. Encouraged, reviewed quit line, he hasn't called yet. Will keep going and see PCP in December.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back on the cigarettes, close to a pack a day again. Did well through mid-November at around 10 a day, then work got busy before the holidays and it crept back. Feels the bupropion isn't doing anything at this point and doesn't want to keep paying for it. Not up for another try right now - maybe after the new year, he says.

No side effects from it. Mood fine.

Vitals as charted.

Plan: stop bupropion. No shame in a relapse; most people need several attempts. Will check in each visit. Ok to restart this or try something else whenever he wants.

Colon cancer screening - he's ready now. Referral to GI for screening colonoscopy, no family history of colon cancer, no symptoms.

documents.title: Colonoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside endoscopy center
Procedure: screening colonoscopy, 03/24/2022
Patient: Eric Strong, 48M
Indication: average-risk colorectal cancer screening
Allergies: NKDA
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care

Prep: good. Cecum reached, identified by appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve. Withdrawal time 9 minutes.

Findings: normal mucosa throughout the colon and rectum. No polyps. Retroflexion in the rectum normal.

Impression: normal screening colonoscopy.
Recommendation: repeat in 10 years. Resume usual medications.

orders.reason: metabolic syndrome, weight gain on olanzapine

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical. 48 y/o.

Interval: colonoscopy in March was normal, next in 10 years. Bupropion stopped in December, smoking a pack a day. Psoriasis quiet with weekend clobetasol. Knee the same, ibuprofen now and then.

Weight is up - 96 kg today, about 7 kg more than in the fall. He doesn't think he's eating any differently. Olanzapine is the same dose it has been for years.

Meds: lisinopril 10, atorvastatin 20, olanzapine 10 qhs, ibuprofen prn, clobetasol oint weekends. NKDA.

ROS negative except as above.

Exam: BP 134/84. Comfortable. HEENT normal. Neck without nodes or thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Knee: crepitus R, no effusion. Skin: a few faint plaques on the elbows. No edema.

A/P
1. Metabolic syndrome with weight gain on an antipsychotic - would like endocrinology's input on the metabolic side. Referral placed. CMP, lipids, CBC today.
2. HTN at goal.
3. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 20.
4. Tobacco: counseled again, not ready.
5. Screening: colon done. PHQ-2 negative.
6. Flu/COVID boosters in the fall.

documents.body: Hi Eric - kidney and liver tests and blood count normal. Fasting sugar 106, slightly above normal. LDL 132, HDL 38, triglycerides 230. These fit with the weight change and are good things for the endocrinologist to look at with you. Their office will call to schedule.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology Clinic
Date of visit: 10/07/2022
Re: Eric Strong, 48 y/o man

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for asking me to see Mr. Strong about the metabolic effects of his olanzapine. He has taken olanzapine for schizophrenia for years, stable, through his psychiatrist, and carries diagnoses of metabolic syndrome, hypertension and hyperlipidemia.

Over the past three months he has been thirsty much of the time and urinating more often, including at night, and has gained about 10 pounds over the same stretch. He has not changed what he eats or how active he is. His mother has type 2 diabetes.

Medications: lisinopril 10 mg once daily, atorvastatin 20 mg once daily, ibuprofen 200-400 mg as needed for knee pain.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: smokes about a pack a day since age 15, roughly 30 pack-years. Social alcohol, 1-2 drinks on weekends. Office manager.

Exam: BP 135/85. BMI 32. He has a cushingoid appearance. Otherwise unremarkable.

Fasting labs this morning: glucose 126 mg/dL and A1c 7.2%. Total cholesterol 230, HDL 35, triglycerides 250, LDL 145 mg/dL.

Assessment:
1. Type 2 diabetes, new, in the setting of olanzapine and metabolic syndrome - antipsychotic-induced. Symptomatic hyperglycemia but A1c 7.2.
2. Obesity, BMI 32.
3. Dyslipidemia, as above.

Plan:
- Metformin 500 mg twice daily with meals; we'll titrate at the next visit.
- Met with our diabetes educator today to go over food choices.
- Return in 3 months with an A1c.

I will keep you informed.

Sincerely,
Endocrinology
